record.provider: Lark / 飞书 Drive via multi-tenant app credentials (the FeiSync pattern)
record.category: platform storage reached through app credentials

free_tier.stated: 100 GB per Lark tenant. '任意扩容，只要添加 App ID 和 App Secret 就可以免费获得100G空间，单文件250M，简单说就是容量上限取决于你的号数量'

retention.stated: While the tenant persists. No retention clock published

egress.terms: Unmetered in practice; there is no egress line item on the free tier

record.tooling: FeiSync v1.0.0 by fish2018, Tauri and Rust with a Vue front end, presented on linux.do on 2025-12-28: multi-tenant routing, one-way or two-way cron sync, resumable transfer and an open HTTP API. The underlying API is the Lark Drive open platform v1 at /drive/v1/files
record.chaining: This is the Google service-account pattern reimplemented for Lark: create N free tenants, register a custom app in each, and FeiSync load-balances writes across them for 100 GB times N in one flat namespace. 250 MB per file is the binding number, not the bytes

limits.value: apps inside one tenant share that tenant's 100 GB, so a second app is not a second quota

identity_cost.detail: a distinct email address or phone number per tenant. Lark has historically required an overseas IP to register outside the mainland, which is a feature here

record.reliability_note: Two constraints bite: 250 MB per file caps the cold-archive case hard, and app-permission changes break the wrapper. Tenant creation needs a distinct identity each time

evidence.proved: '免费无限扩容，每个账号免费扩容100G，单文件250M' and '不能是同一个企业的不同应用，会共享100G'
'larksuite所谓飞书海外版，必须要海外IP才能注册'; '海外ip，会成功'
'Lark 免费用户就有自定域名邮箱、100 GB 存储'

record.notes: The most directly applicable of the app-credential patterns, because tenancy is free and self-service. The 250 MB file cap is what makes it a shard target rather than a store, and that is a job for a chunker rather than a blocker.

aliases: Lark / 飞书 Drive via multi-tenant app credentials (FeiSync pattern)

card.summary: 100 GB total storage per organization on Starter (Free); 250 MB single-file limit for Docs uploads on Starter

free_tier.stated: 100 GB total storage per organization on Starter (Free); 250 MB single-file limit for Docs uploads on Starter

egress.terms: Downloads served from Lark CDN (ByteDance edge) at no metered charge; download via OpenAPI media download returns a signed URL, no per-GB line item anywhere in the plan table

record.tooling: Official OpenAPI v3 drive endpoints (upload_all for <=20MB, multipart upload of 4MB chunks above that) + first-party CLI larksuite/cli (17,762 stars, pushed 2026-10-21) with `lark-cli drive +upload`; no rclone backend
record.chaining: 100 GB x N free organizations. Starter is self-serve per organization and the quota is per-org, not per-user, so N disposable orgs = N x 100 GB. Paid Basic (5 TB) shows the ceiling is only billing, not architecture.
record.limits_note: 250 MB per file for Docs on Starter (vs 50 GB on Pro); upload_all hard-caps at 20 MB by design, must use multipart; 5 QPS on upload_all; 4 MB fixed chunk size on multipart; upload transaction ID valid 1 day for resume
record.reliability_note: Rate limits are explicit (5 QPS on single upload) and multipart is resumable, but Starter orgs that lapse back from a paid plan are force-collapsed to Starter member and storage caps - data above 100 GB becomes unwritable, not deleted.

evidence.proved: table row: 'Total storage space | 100 GB | 5 TB | 15 TB | 15 TB + 30 GB x purchased seats'; 'Single file upload limit for Docs | 250 MB'
'please do not use this interface to upload files larger than 20MB... use the multipart upload interface', supports 5QPS

record.notes: 100 GB total storage per organization on Starter (Free); 250 MB single-file limit for Docs uploads on Starter
